subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: What Signal edit behavior should OpenClaw own now: a Signal-local edit path, a narrower marker-only path, or deferral until the cross-channel source-message lifecycle contract is designed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but transcript replacement, dedupe identity, and whether edits should trigger replies are product semantics rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Signal-local edit path
options.body: Add Signal-specific `targetSentTimestamp` handling, edit metadata or marker, dedupe/transcript replacement, and mention-gated reply suppression while leaving cross-channel cancel semantics to the umbrella lifecycle issue.

options.title: Marker-only first step
options.body: Accept a smaller Signal plugin change that marks edited content and uses the target timestamp for identity, but does not replace transcript history yet.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this blocked until the broader source-message edit/delete/recall lifecycle issue defines shared semantics across channels.

recommendation.title: Signal-local edit path
recommendation.body: Add Signal-specific `targetSentTimestamp` handling, edit metadata or marker, dedupe/transcript replacement, and mention-gated reply suppression while leaving cross-channel cancel semantics to the umbrella lifecycle issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current-main history is in the Signal inbound runtime path and recent event-handler refactors.
